title: Shift debrief & follow-ups (on-call) - 2026-03-21
content:
Quick overview

Purpose: compact handoff for next shift with incident summaries, immediate mitigations, and outstanding follow-ups. Intended to be scanned in 5-7 minutes.

Shift window: 2026-03-21 18:00 - 2026-03-21 23:59 PT (US-west ops). Night coverage picks up at 00:00 UTC — handoff at 23:30 PT.

People
- On-call: Aisha Patel (primary)
- Secondary: Diego Marquez (infra)
- Rotation shadow: June Park (learning shift)
- Notified: Ravi Singh (SRE lead) for high-sev incidents

Summary (top-line)
- One high-sev incident (INC-2026-031) tied to model-serving autoscale regressions; partial fallback to small-ram model variant activated.
- Two medium incidents: transient Redis auth failures causing cache misses; and elevated p99 latency on hosted-api/chat route during traffic spike at ~21:10 PT.
- No data exfiltration, no customer data loss. No contractual SLA breach expected but ops ticket opened to track SLA exposure window.

Incident: INC-2026-031 — autoscale regression
- Time window: 20:58 - 21:42 PT
- Symptoms: sudden drop in available GPU workers for rtx-8000 pool; controller reported scale-down events not triggered by policy. Throttled requests increased, queue backlog rose, per-token latency increased ~4x.
- Immediate mitigation: Manually increased desired_count on the worker pool and triggered warmup sequence; routed new requests to dedicated fallback pool (model-rd_small_v2) via routing policy override. Short-term config change: increased scale-up aggressiveness by temporarily setting cooldown to 30s (was 120s).
- Root cause hypothesis: regression in new controller release (svc-controller v2.11.0) that introduced a race between termination hook and autoscaler health-check. New release deployed earlier in the day at 14:10 PT.
- Evidence: controller logs show rapid sequence of TerminatePod -> PodNotReady events; autoscaler saw repeated false-negative readiness checks. Repro steps queued in SRE-8721.
- Customer impact: elevated latency for ~44 minutes for hosted inference customers in us-west. Some requests served by fallback model variant with slightly lower throughput but acceptable quality (notified product).
- Action items (assigned):
  - Diego: roll back controller to v2.10.4 on canary nodes and monitor for 1h (JIRA SRE-8721).
  - Aisha: add a temporary canary alert rule to detect >30% scale-down in 5m window to trigger an automated rollback hook.
  - Ravi: schedule post-incident RCA and coordinate with release engineering to hold v2.11.0 in staging until fix.

Medium: Redis auth flaps
- Time window: intermittent 19:15 - 22:20 PT
- Symptoms: AUTH errors from application nodes to redis-hot leading to cache bypass and DB read amplification. Affected mostly lower priority jobs (metrics ingestion, some non-critical embedding cache).
- Immediate mitigation: rotated redis static credential key used by non-prod pools; restarted 3 client pods to pick up credentials. Added short-term retry/backoff to the client library config.
- Probable cause: short-lived bug in secret rotation service that attempted to push a placeholder token to older clusters. Follow-up: engineering/secrets to audit rotation logic.
- Action items:
  - June: add extra metrics for redis auth failures and change incident title format to include "auth" for easier paging.
  - Aisha: coordinate with secrets team on a postmortem; include evidence and timeline.

Performance note: p99 latency spike on /v1/chat
- Observed: 21:07 PT — sustained p99 increase from 280ms -> 1.2s for ~20m, correlated with autoscale regression.
- Rooted to queue backlog and increased host swap in the worker pool. No code change observed at that timestamp.
- Temporary config: increased request concurrency threshold per worker from 16 -> 24 to allow higher throughput (temporary; scheduled to revert after 2 hours).
- Action: Add a synthetic test that exercises long-tail prompts at 2x production rate during autoscale event testing. (Assigned to Perf team, ticket PERF-319).

Runbook gaps surfaced
- Runbook: "worker-autoscale-failures.md" lacks guidance on rapid rollback vs temporary routing overrides. It also assumes gaussian traffic; doesn't document cooldown interplay with termination hooks.
- Quick edits we made: appended a short checklist under "Immediate mitigations" for tonight (manual adjust desired_count, verify readiness probes, route to fallback model).
- Action: Create an RFC to formalize autoscaler safety checks and rollback TTL. (Owner: Ravi; due: 2026-03-28).

Outstanding follow-ups (priority ordered)
1) SRE-8721: controller rollback + canary validation (Diego) — high priority, due 2026-03-22 12:00 PT.
2) Secrets rotation postmortem and patch (SecretOps & Aisha) — medium, due 2026-03-24.
3) Runbook expansion for autoscaler + termination hook interplay (Ravi) — medium, due 2026-03-28.
4) Temporary concurrency change revert audit (Perf & Infra) — low, due 2026-03-22 06:00 PT.
5) Synthetic p99 long-tail test + CI gating for autoscale releases (Perf) — medium, due 2026-04-05.

Notes for next shift
- If you see controller-scale anomalies: immediately set routing override to fallback-models and notify Release Eng. Do NOT wait for full queue saturation. Use the emergency runbook snippet (page: /pages/viewpage.action?pageId=66789012#Emergency-Runbook).
- Watch for Redis auth errors in logs: metric name redis.client.auth.failures, threshold >5/m triggers pager. If triggered, try rotating the non-production key first to reduce blast radius.
- Keep an eye on canary nodes (label: canary=true) to see if controller behavior differs — we saw first failure on a canary node.

Misc operational items
- Patch window planned: 2026-03-23 02:00 PT for infra network maintenance. On-call will be notified 24h in advance.
- Monthly capacity review: slack poll sent to infra@ for updated GPU headroom numbers.
- Documentation: I added a brief screenshot of the controller logs to SRE-8721 and a short timeline in the Jira ticket.

Open questions
- Should the routing override policy include an automated quality-check for fallback models before switching at scale? (pg: product-hosted-api input needed)
- Do we want an automated rollback hook on controller upgrades if readiness probe failures spike beyond baseline? (Ravi to propose in RFC)

Appendix: Short log excerpts (copied raw)
- controller.log 20:59:12 PT: "pod terminate invoked uid=pod-97fa; readiness_probe=false; marking unschedulable"
- autoscaler.log 20:59:15 PT: "scaledown_decision: true; last_scale_time=20:57:03; scale_in_cooldown=120s"
- worker-rtx-01 21:03:40 PT: "evicting KV cache entry due to memory_pressure"

Quick checklist for handoff (to paste into Slack)
- [ ] Confirm rollback status on SRE-8721
- [ ] Ensure routing override is still active (if not already reverted)
- [ ] Verify redis.client.auth.failures < 1/m for 30m
- [ ] Revert temporary concurrency tweak if stable
- [ ] Ping Release Eng + Product about impact note

If anything urgent pops up overnight, page me (Aisha) or Diego. Leaving detailed notes in JIRA SRE-8721 and Confluence quick page.

End of shift — Aisha
